full_judgment: 8. The learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner has argued that all the above mentioned ingredients for constituting adverse possession though present in this case but inspite of that the Revisional Court held that the defendant No.1 could not acquire any title in the land in question by adverse possession. The learned Advocate has argued also that the Appellate Court and also the Revisional Court committed wrong in holding that the defendant No.1 did not claim a case of adverse possession; that the defendant's continuous possession for more than 20 years in assertion of his own right and title and denying the title of the plaintiffs has already created his title in this land and has also extinguished plaintiffs right and title therein as per section 28 of the Limitation Act and in the circumstances the alleged non making of plea of adverse possession by the defendant No.1 does not matter at all.
